item.title: Hierarchical design strategies for tuning genetic circuits.
item.abstract: Genetic circuit design is central to synthetic biology, yet achieving predictable and programmable circuit performance remains challenging due to diverse circuit- and host-dependent factors. Thus, a systematic perspective is needed to integrate these factors across multiple design layers. In this review, we establish a hierarchical framework for tuning genetic circuits as an engineering process spanning biological part design, DNA synthesis and assembly, carrier selection, host-cell implementation, and cross-host transfer. We further discuss how each layer contributes to circuit behavior and shapes trade-offs among key performance properties. By integrating hierarchical design strategies with iterative troubleshooting, this review provides a practical roadmap for tuning genetic circuits toward more predictable and reliable performance.

item.title: Prime Editing: Mechanism and Developments.
item.abstract: Prime editing is a "search and replace" based genome editing method that can introduce point mutations, insertions, and deletions into DNA at desired sites, making it the editing technique capable of making the most diverse range of edits. Prime editing utilizes a Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase to introduce edits encoded by a specially designed DNA oligonucleotide called a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA). While prime editing has been shown to achieve robust editing in different genomic loci and in different cell types, this technology still has the potential for further optimization and improvement. Many groups have been successful in improving prime editing outcomes by optimizing the design of prime editors and pegRNAs. Additionally, modulating key cellular pathways has also been an effective tool for achieving high levels of editing. Due to its high efficiency and relative safety, prime editing has the potential to transform disease modeling and genomic medicine.

item.title: On-demand biomanufacturing via programmed SporeBot.
item.abstract: Biopharmaceuticals, including antimicrobial peptides and engineered protein-based vaccines, represent key products of the biotechnology sector. However, their reliance on large-scale manufacturing and cold-chain logistics limits deployment in field and resource-limited settings. To address this gap, we developed SporeBot, a platform that exploits the intrinsic stability of Bacillus subtilis spores for versatile and on-demand biopharmaceutical production. The platform comprises polymeric microcapsules that encapsulate engineered spores. These spores exhibit robust stability, retaining engineered functionality under harsh conditions and extended storage. Upon activation, germinated cells secrete the target proteins, which diffuse across a polymeric mesh that physically separates the cellular factory from the secreted product. We validate this platform through the production and functional testing of antimicrobial peptides and vaccine antigens. Our approach resolves key manufacturing and distribution constraints of protein therapeutics and offers a deployable solution for on-demand biomanufacturing in both developed and resource-limited settings.

item.title: Large Insertion Using Template-Jumping Prime Editing.
item.abstract: Prime editors (PEs) are advanced gene-editing tools capable of a wide spectrum of genomic modifications, offering significant potential for gene therapy. The template-jumping prime editing (TJ-PE) system employs template-jumping prime editing guide RNAs (TJ-pegRNAs) with a dual primer binding site (PBS) sequence. One PBS anneals to the DNA flap generated by the TJ-pegRNA, while the other binds to the DNA flap generated by the nicking sgRNA, enabling the accurate insertion of large DNA fragments.

item.title: Emerging synthetic biology toolkits to control gene expression and provide therapeutic avenues in cardiovascular disease.
item.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Synthetic biology is an emerging field that integrates engineering principles, molecular innovations, interdisciplinary methodologies, and designer toolkits to create versatile and adaptable platforms for control, enhance, and reprogram signaling, phenotype, or function in biological systems and living organisms. Advances in mammalian synthetic biology have generated growing interest in its translational applications, including cardiovascular drug discovery and disease management.
AREAS COVERED: This concise report highlights promising synthetic biology-inspired technologies that have been applied or can potentially apply to transgene regulation and disease management in cardiovascular medicine, such as tunable regulatory switches, programmable gene circuits, synthetic sensing modules, and gut-heart axis engineering. We also summarize recent translational progress in the field and discuss remaining obstacles, potential solutions, and future opportunities, with particular emphasis on the progression from laboratory concepts to practical applications in cardiovascular disease.
EXPERT OPINION: Synthetic biology is steadily advancing toward translation. However, barriers for clinical implementation remain, including non‑mammalian components, immunogenicity, regulatory uncertainty, and broader ethical and safety concerns. Emerging solutions, including humanized molecular components, advanced monitoring strategies, and machine learning, may help mitigate those risks and expand the cardiovascular utility of synthetic biology. Stronger evidence and deeper clinical integration will position the field for future cardiovascular medicine.

item.title: Design of Highly Efficient pegRNAs with Minimized Off-Target Effects Using DeepPrime.
item.abstract: Prime editors are newly developed genome editing tools capable of installing various types of mutations without introducing double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs) or requiring donor DNA templates. Prime editors consist of a Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase (RT) domain and function as a ribonucleoprotein complex with prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA). Unlike the single guide RNA (sgRNA) used with Cas9 or base editors, the editing efficiency of pegRNAs is determined by the sequence composition and length of the guide sequence, primer binding site (PBS), and reverse transcription template (RTT). The high design flexibility of pegRNAs presents both opportunities and challenges. Therefore, designing pegRNAs with high efficacy has been a significant hurdle for the application of prime editing. Here, we present a step-by-step protocol for designing optimal pegRNAs to introduce desired edits using a deep learning-based algorithm, DeepPrime.

item.title: Protocol for Prime Editing with Engineered PAM-Flexible Cas9 Variants.
item.abstract: Prime editing (PE) is a precision genome-editing technology that allows all types of editing, such as substitutions, insertions, and deletions, at the target site in the genome of a cell without double-strand breaks (DSBs) or donor DNA. However, the targeting range of existing prime editing systems is limited due to their dependence on the NGG protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) recognized by Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (spCas9). To address this limitation, we have engineered prime editor variants incorporating PAM-flexible Cas9 proteins. These variants significantly expand the range of targetable genomic sites, allowing for the introduction of mutations previously inaccessible to standard editing methods. Here, we provide detailed methods for applying these PAM-flexible PE variants in human cell lines.

item.title: TAPE-seq: A Cell-Based Method for Genome-Wide Off-Target Prediction in Prime Editing.
item.abstract: Prime editors are powerful genome-editing tools that enables precise sequence modifications without the need for double-strand breaks or donor DNA templates. Given their distinct mechanism of action, evaluating their off-target activities is essential for ensuring safety in ongoing clinical development. Unlike Cas9-based tools that predict off-target effects indirectly, TAPE-seq directly leverages PE activity to map genome-wide off-target sites with high sensitivity and specificity. This detailed protocol provides a robust framework for evaluating the safety of PE-based genome-editing applications.

item.title: Construction of the p2PE3 Platform Based on RNA-Pol-II-Driven Engineered pegRNA.
item.abstract: Prime editor (PE) is a versatile tool capable of precisely installing programmed genetic information into eukaryotic genomes. The canonical PE3 system uses a constitutive RNA polymerase III (RNA-Pol-III) promoter to drive RNA expression. However, RNA-Pol-III is unable to efficiently transcribe RNA sequences containing poly(T) motifs or gRNAs expressed in tandem, which restricts the application of PE. Here, we detail the use of an RNA polymerase II (RNA-Pol-II) promoter to drive RNA expression, coupled with Csy4 for RNA processing. This approach enabled efficient editing with poly(T)-containing pegRNAs, multiple gRNA editing combinations, and conditionally inducible gRNA. These findings overcome the limitations of RNA-Pol-III-driven RNA systems and broaden the applications of prime editing.

item.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
item.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing structure-based functional assignments for uncharacterized proteins and verifying the accuracy of annotations previously generated by protein sequence homology analysis alone. Using a combination of precomputed structures from the AlphaFold Database and newly generated AlphaFold 3 structural predictions, we produced high-confidence predicted structural models for approximately 92% of the TPANIC proteome, enabling us to identify structural homologs and assign potential functional annotations to 24 previously uncharacterized proteins. Beyond functional annotation, the updated genome-derived structural models revealed several major structural revisions resulting from corrected gene models. Most notably, integration of comparative structural analyses and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling redefined the composition of the TPA outer membrane biogenesis machinery, supporting the existence of a conserved spirochete-specific BAM-TAM complex containing BamA, TamB, BamD, and BamB. We anticipate that the resulting AlphaFold protein structure atlas, in combination with the recently developed tools of in vitro cultivation and genetic manipulation, will help elucidate the roles of TPANIC proteins in the organism's biology, pathogenesis, and host immune interactions.IMPORTANCEIncidence of syphilis has been on the rise in the past decade, emphasizing the need to understand the mechanisms behind the persistence and virulence of its causative agent, Treponema pallidum. In this study, we employed a next-generation artificial intelligence-based protein structure modeling and matching pipeline, building upon prior structural conservation studies by expanding the functional predictions for hypothetical proteins. Consequently, this study provides a clearer picture of the metabolic and pathogenic capabilities of this elusive pathogen, while highlighting the intricacies of its regulatory landscape. We anticipate that our strategy will complement existing sequence-homology-based gene/genome annotation pipelines, assisting in both protein function validation and the identification of orthologous proteins lacking sequence homology.

item.title: Improvement of Genome Editing Efficiency in Mammalian Cells by a Refined Uni-Vector Prime Editing System.
item.abstract: Prime editing is an advanced technology in the CRISPR/Cas genome editing field. The original multi-vector method utilized in prime editing has less efficiency and precision and is also inherently difficult in generating homozygous mutations in mammalian cells. To overcome these technical difficulties, a Uni-vector prime editing system containing the major components for prime editing has been constructed in two all-in-one plasmids, pPE3-pPuro and pePE5max-pPuro. The Uni-vector prime editing plasmids enhance the editing efficiency of prime editing and improve the generation of homozygous mutated mammalian cell lines. The editing efficiency depends on the transfection efficiency. Remarkably, the Uni-vector ePE5max system can achieve a high editing rate even in cell lines that are traditionally difficult to transfect. This Uni-vector approach simplifies the delivery of all the necessary editing components and greatly improves the editing efficiency. This approach represents an advanced progress in the field of prime editing.

item.title: Optimization and Evaluation of Prime Editing Activity in Human iPSCs.
item.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) retain the genetic information of their donors, making them invaluable for modeling genetic diseases and for isogenic controls. Precise genome editing in iPSCs is essential to realizing this potential. However, efficient precision editing of iPSCs remains challenging due to the lack of direct enrichment strategies for edited cells carrying subtle mutations such as small insertions and deletions (indels) or single-nucleotide variants (SNVs). Previously, we demonstrated that fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) can indirectly enrich cells with ssODN-templated edits by selecting those with high plasmid-based co-expression of Cas9 and mCherry. While effective, editing approaches relying on Cas9-induced double-strand breaks (DSBs) increase the risk of on-target byproducts, emphasizing the need for alternative strategies. Prime editing offers DSB-free precision editing by using a Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase to install edits encoded in prime editing guide RNAs (pegRNAs). Here, we present both plasmid-based and mRNA-based prime editing protocols to generate precise edits evaluated using a GFP-to-BFP conversion assay. The plasmid method is cost-effective and allows for FACS-based enrichment of edited cells, while the mRNA method minimizes genomic integration risk while improving editing efficiencies without the need for enrichment. Together, these methods provide robust platforms for efficient precision editing in human iPSCs, facilitating downstream functional genomics and therapeutic applications.

item.title: Rapid Cell-Free Preparation of Circular Vector DNA for pegRNA Expression in Prime Editing.
item.abstract: The expression of prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) is crucial for effective CRISPR-Cas9 prime genome editing, traditionally facilitated by DNA plasmids, which require a time-consuming process of bacterial cloning, validation, and purification. The Circular Vector (CV) protocol represents an efficient, fully synthetic, cell-free method that bypasses these traditional steps, allowing for the preparation of pegRNA expression vectors within 3 h. This approach involves circularizing and purifying linear double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) templates containing a promoter with pegRNA elements into compact, bacterial-backbone-free vectors. These CVs offer significant advantages: absence of a bacterial backbone, absence of endotoxins, and no contamination by bacterial nucleic acids, making them a superior choice for transfection in cell culture experiments, where they have shown performance equal to or better than that of traditional plasmids. The CV protocol not only speeds up the preparation process but also reduces costs and complexity, making it an ideal tool for rapid and efficient pegRNA expression in research settings.

item.title: PE-STOP for Precise Installation/Reversion of Nonsense Mutation.
item.abstract: PE-STOP is a versatile tool suited for precise installation of nonsense mutations. With high degrees of adaptability, it facilitates gene inactivation and the construction of ClinVar-recorded nonsense mutations. Based on the safe PE platform, PE-STOP circumvents numerous complications associated with conventional gene inactivation approaches dependent on double-strand DNA break (DSB) generation. Compared to other DSB-independent tools like iSTOP and i-Silence, PE-STOP offers enhanced target specificity, single-nucleotide precision, and much greater site coverage. Here, we describe the effective use of PE-STOP to introduce stop codons in human embryonic kidney 293 T cells, which may be followed by a subsequent round of precise in situ editing to rescue nonsense mutations via the PE platform.

cards.title_cn: PE-STOP：精准引入与回复无义突变
cards.one_liner: PE-STOP 基于先导编辑平台，可精准引入无义突变，并能在原位回复该突变。
key_findings: 利用 PE 平台在 HEK293T 细胞中精准引入终止密码子，实现基因失活。
相比 iSTOP、i-Silence 等不依赖 DSB 的工具，靶向特异性更高、可覆盖位点更多。
可构建 ClinVar 收录的无义突变，并支持后续原位精准回复。
cards.why_it_matters: 为基因失活与无义突变疾病建模提供不依赖双链断裂的精准工具，契合合成生物学中基因线路调控与疾病模型构建需求。
